items.question: What is the 2025 IRT exemption threshold in Angola?

items.answer: Yes, Angolan labor law mandates a 13th-month salary (Christmas bonus) and a vacation bonus, each equal to one month's base salary.

items.question: How are vacation days calculated?

items.question: Is there a minimum wage update for 2025?
items.answer: The minimum wage was significantly increased in late 2024; businesses should budget for at least AOA 70,000 to AOA 100,000 depending on the sector.

items.question: What is SAF-T (AO)?
items.answer: It is a standardized XML file capturing accounting and invoicing data that must be submitted to the AGT portal monthly.

services.name: M & A
services.description: Detailed information about M&A Services in Angola.

content.markdown:
### M&A Financials

Mergers and Acquisitions in Angola are concentrated in the energy, banking, and retail sectors. Advisory fees usually follow a 'Success Fee' model (Lehman Formula or similar) plus fixed retainers for due diligence and legal structuring.

steps.title: Target Screening & NDA
steps.description: Identify local targets and execute Portuguese/English bilingual Non-Disclosure Agreements.

steps.title: Valuation & Letter of Intent
steps.description: Perform DCF and Multiples analysis, adjusting for Angolan country risk premiums (ERP).

steps.title: Integrated Due Diligence
steps.description: Deep dive into Tax (AGT), Social Security (INSS), and historical labor litigation.

steps.title: Regulatory Notification
steps.description: Notify AIPEX and relevant sector regulators (e.g., BNA for finance) of the change in control.

steps.title: SPA Execution & Closing
steps.description: Finalize the Share purchase Agreement (SPA) and handle local notary requirements for title transfer.

steps.title: Post-Merger Integration
steps.description: Harmonize payroll, HRIS systems, and cultural alignment under Law 12/23.

content.markdown:
### Deal Timeline

- Phase 1: Preparation & Sourcing (1–2 months)
- Phase 2: Due Diligence (1–3 months)
- Phase 3: Closing & Regulatory (2–4 months)

items.title: Asset vs Share Deals
items.text: Share deals are more common but require exhaustive historical tax due diligence. Asset deals can mitigate legacy liabilities.

items.title: Forex Risk
items.text: Currency devaluations (Kwanza vs USD) can rapidly shift the effective deal value between signing and closing.

items.title: Local Partner Value
items.text: In regulated sectors, maintaining a local minority shareholder can flatten the curve for regulatory approvals.

items.title: Central Bank (BNA) Clause
items.text: Transactions involving significant foreign currency transfers require explicit PRI (Private Investment) registration to allow future dividend exits.

content.markdown: M&A in Angola is currently driven by privatization programs (PROPRIV) and consolidation in the oil service sector. Success hinges on a 'local-first' due diligence approach that prioritizes checking the 'frozen' status of target NIFs before any capital commitment.

items.question: Can a foreign company acquire 100% of an Angolan firm?
items.answer: Yes, in most sectors. However, strategic sectors like Oil, Mining, and Defense often have specific local partnership requirements.

items.question: How long does due diligence typically take in Angola?
items.answer: Expect 8–12 weeks. Data rooms are often physical or semi-digital, and verifying bank/AGT standings requires local physical visits.

items.question: Is the Lehman Formula used for advisory fees?
items.answer: Yes, many boutique firms use the 5-4-3-2-1% formula or a flat 2-3% for mid-market deals.

items.question: What is the role of AIPEX in an acquisition?
items.answer: AIPEX must approve the transfer of an existing Investment Project (CRIP) to a new owner to maintain tax incentives.

items.question: Are 'Vendor Due Diligence' reports common?
items.answer: Increasingly so for larger transactions, but most buyers still insist on independent 'Buy-Side' due diligence.

items.question: How do you handle 'Hidden Liabilities' in Angola?
items.answer: Robust SPA warranties and indemnities are used, but escrow accounts (locally or offshore) are the preferred mitigation tool.

items.question: What is PROPRIV?
items.answer: The Privatization Program of the Angolan Government, offering opportunities to acquire interests in state-owned enterprises (SOEs).

services.name: Software & Technology Solutions
services.description: Detailed information about Software Solutions in Angola.

content.markdown:
### Tech Service Financials

Software development in Angola is a growing sector, with Luanda becoming a hub for fintech and logistics startups. Offshore-onshore hybrid models are common, where strategy is global but implementation is localized for internet latency and language (Portuguese).

steps.title: Discovery & Localization Audit
steps.description: Evaluate UI/UX for Portuguese nuances and Angolan payment gateway integrations (MCX).

steps.title: Sprint Planning (Agile)
steps.description: Establish bi-weekly milestones with local project managers to navigate Luanda's infrastructure challenges.

steps.title: Development & APD Compliance
steps.description: Build features while ensuring data handling complies with Angolan Data Protection Law.

steps.title: Local UAT & Performance Testing
steps.description: Test applications against local internet speeds and 'Unitel/Movicel' network constraints.

steps.title: Production Deployment
steps.description: Set up production environments in local IDCs or approved global clouds (Azure/AWS).

steps.title: Support & Maintenance
steps.description: Establish a Portuguese-speaking first-line support desk for local corporate users.

content.markdown:
### Technical Stack

Modern Angolan startups favor Typescript/React and Python/Django, with a strong emphasis on cross-platform mobile frameworks like Flutter to reach consumers.

items.title: Data Residency
items.text: For specific sectors like Banking and Oil, the APD may require critical data to be mirrored or hosted within Angolan borders.

items.title: API Maturity
items.text: Many local institutions (MCX, AGT) have evolving API documentation; ensure your dev team has 'boots on the ground' to verify implementation.

items.title: Progressive Web Apps (PWA)
items.text: Due to variable data costs and connectivity, PWAs are often more effective for broad consumer reach than heavy native apps.

items.title: Certified Billing Software
items.text: Any B2B software must integrate with AGT-certified invoicing modules as per SAF-T AO regulations.

content.markdown: The 'Digitalization of Angola' is a government priority. Success requires moving beyond simple 'lift-and-shift' of global software, focusing instead on optimizing for the local infrastructure and the specific 2024 tax/labor law logic.

items.question: Does my software developer need to be in Luanda?
items.answer: Not for coding, but for requirements gathering and UAT, having someone local is critical for navigating local payment and tax integrations.

items.question: What is MCX (Multicaixa Express)?
items.answer: It is the dominant domestic card network and mobile payment platform; almost all Angolan E-commerce requires MCX integration.

items.question: Is cloud hosting available in Angola?
items.answer: Yes, providers like Angola Cables and ITA offer high-quality Tier III data center facilities in Luanda.

items.question: Are there tax incentives for tech startups?
items.answer: Qualified tech companies can apply for significant Industrial Tax exemptions via AIPEX if they demonstrate local R&D.

items.question: How do you handle software licensing payments?
items.answer: Paying for foreign licenses (SaaS) requires BNA approval for forex exit; use local resellers where possible to pay in Kwanza.

items.question: What is the standard for Digital Signatures in Angola?
items.answer: Law 12/23 recognizes digital signatures, but they must comply with the National Electronic Certification infrastructure (INFOSI).

items.question: Can I hire remote developers from Portugal?
items.answer: Yes, this is very common due to the shared language and legal heritage, but expect to pay higher rates than local Luanda talent.

services.name: MARKETING AGENCY
services.description: Detailed information about Marketing Agencies in Angola.

content.markdown:
### Marketing Financials

Marketing in Angola is a mix of high-digital engagement in Luanda and traditional 'Out-of-Home' (OOH) media in provinces. Costs vary significantly between local boutique agencies and international full-service firms.

steps.title: Angolan Consumer Profile
steps.description: Analyze purchasing power across Luanda and key provinces like Benguela and Huambo.

steps.title: Channel Optimization
steps.description: Select between Facebook/Instagram (dominant) and high-visibility physical street marketing.

steps.title: Content Production (Bilingual)
steps.description: Develop assets in Portuguese, ensuring cultural relevance and local idiom usage.

steps.title: Media Buy Execution
steps.description: Negotiate placements with local media houses (TPA, TV Zimbo) and billboard owners.

steps.title: Performance Tracking
steps.description: Monitor engagement metrics and lead conversion, adjusting for local mobile data costs.

content.markdown:
### Strategic Reach

- Digital: Focused on Luanda's youth and middle class (40% penetration).
- OOH: Essential for mass market brand recognition across the 18 provinces.

items.title: The 'Facebook' Internet
items.text: For many Angolans, Facebook is 'The Internet'. Meta-centric strategies outperform Google Search due to zero-rating data plans.

items.title: Ad Clearance
items.text: Specific industries like Pharma, Alcohol, and Finance require prior approval from sectoral regulators for TV/Radio ads.

items.title: Radio is King
items.text: Outside Luanda, Radio remains the most trusted and widely heard medium for over 70% of the population.

items.title: Portuguese Nuance
items.text: Standard European Portuguese can feel 'stiff'. Using 'Angolanismos' (local slang) builds significant brand trust.

content.markdown: Marketing in 2025 is trending toward 'Community Commerce'. Brands that leverage local Luanda influencers and WhatsApp groups see the highest conversion rates, as peer recommendation is the primary driver of purchase in the informal economy.

items.question: Which social media platform is most used in Angola?
items.answer: Facebook is the clear leader, followed by WhatsApp and Instagram. TikTok is growing rapidly among the under-25 demographic.

items.question: Do I need a local agency to buy media?
items.answer: While not legally mandatory, local agencies have the relationships to secure better rates and premium billboard spots that 'global' buy-desks cannot access.

items.question: What is the official language for advertising?
items.answer: Portuguese is mandatory for all formal marketing, though local languages (Umbundu, Kimbundu) are often used in rural radio for inclusivity.

items.question: How do you track ROI in the 'Informal Market'?
items.answer: Tracking is challenging; many brands use dedicated WhatsApp numbers or coupon codes in ads to attribute sales to specific physical campaigns.

items.question: Are there restrictions on foreign brands?
items.answer: No specific restrictions, but all imported marketing materials must be declared and the content must respect 'Angolan Sovereignty' and cultural norms.

items.question: What is 'Street Marketing' in Angola?
items.answer: It involves 'Activations'—highly energetic physical events in markets (Praças) with music and live demonstrations to drive immediate sales.

items.question: Can I pay for Facebook ads in Kwanza?
items.answer: Most international platforms require 'Cartão Multicaixa' enabled for international web payments, subject to the user's USD limit.
